$comment: The Contributor Community (/contributing/; /roles/, /pin/ and /contributors/ redirect here). Unlisted (noindex, and not linked from the program page) until the board approves it; the home page's Share path leads here, as the explainer for contributing. The one idea: every Lab is built by the people who learn in it. Everyone builds: every role works hands-on in OLOS, building with AI and working through review, because that's baseline now. Each Lab runs its own fork of OLOS. The gold (brass) pin is graduation: you learned enough to build something, it was reviewed and merged into the Lab's OLOS, and the Lab runs on it. Stewards (Reviewer, Committer, Maintainer) run the review, by invitation once you ask. The best of a Lab's work is proposed to the core, the national level of the same system (the nickel pin). The page is three chapters: Learn to build it (every role builds, how work gets in), Graduate (the gold pin, stewards, active or emeritus), Every Lab (the core, what stays true). Plan: docs/contributing-rework-plan.md. Roles are examples, still being worked out, and a Lab can make its own. [PLACEHOLDER] marks what's still open. The covers reuse the program page's macro shots of the pin (src/components/JoinCover.astro): chapters[].shot picks the shot (join.json mission[n]); title is this page's tagline.

meta.need: As someone in a Lab, I need to know how I learn to build, how my work gets into the Lab and beyond, and how that's recognized, so that I can take part in shaping it.

title: Contributor Community
description: Every Lab is built by the people who learn in it. Build it in the Lab near you, prove it there, and the best of it ends up in every Lab.
draft: A working draft. The board hasn't approved this yet, roles are still being worked out, and the pins are still being made.

title: Contributor
Community
hero.lede: Every Lab is built by the people who learn in it. Build it in the Lab near you. Prove it there. The best of it ends up in every Lab.
hero.status: The first pins go to our two steering committees
hero.pinAlt: The gold pin, turning to follow your pointer

why.title: A community you can actually show up to.

items.label: In person
items.title: Close to home.
items.body: People from your own neighborhood, face to face. Not just a chat window.

items.label: Side by side
items.title: Beginners and experts, together.
items.body: Learn from people who've done it. Then teach what you know.

items.label: Hands-on
items.title: Building is the baseline.
items.body: Building with AI and working on shared things through review is becoming as basic as email. You'll learn it here, by doing it.

items.label: Local
items.title: Real problems, real neighbors.
items.body: What you make helps someone you might pass on the street.

start.title: Whatever you run, you'll help build it too.
start.lede: Every Lab runs on OLOS, its own copy of The Labs' shared system. Every role works in it. Running a pod or a chapter is how you find out what needs improving. Building is how you improve it.

items.label: Chapter lead
items.title: Run the Lab.
items.body: And shape how it runs: the playbook, the calendar, the way new people find their footing.

items.label: Experience lead
items.title: Run the room.
items.body: And build the workshops: the agenda, the materials, the parts that worked better the fifth time.

items.label: Poderator
items.title: Run a pod.
items.body: And improve how pods run: forming teams, keeping them moving, getting them to a finished build.

items.label: Community manager
items.title: Bring people together.
items.body: And build how they find each other: the welcome, the follow-up, the way people stay in touch.

start.note: These are examples, and we're still working roles out. The Lab near you might come up with a new one. Whatever the role, you'll learn to build with AI and to collaborate through review, and you won't learn it alone: we'll teach the skills, pair you up, and celebrate your first contribution loudly. [PLACEHOLDER: link to the first guided contribution]

how.title: Have an idea? Show us.
how.lede: You don't have to wait for someone else to do it. You don't hand your workshop to someone and hope it gets added. You learn to put it in yourself.

steps.title: Build it.
steps.body: A tool, a guide, a workshop, a better way to run a pod. Build it with AI, in the Lab's OLOS.

steps.title: Try it.
steps.body: Use it with a pod or at a workshop, and see what happens.

steps.title: Propose it.
steps.body: Put it forward as a change, and work it through review with people in the Lab.

steps.title: It's in.
steps.body: Merged into the Lab's OLOS. The Lab runs on it now, with your name on it.

how.note: Nothing goes in unreviewed, and no one acts alone. But the work, and the credit for it, are yours.

rings.kicker: The pin, and the people who look after it
rings.title: Graduate. Then, if you want to, look after it.
rings.lede: The gold pin means you've graduated: you learned enough to build something, it was reviewed and merged, and the Lab runs on it. Stewards run the review. Each steward role adds a ring behind the pin.

steps.line: You learned to build, and the Lab runs on something you built.
steps.how: Something you built was reviewed and merged into the Lab's OLOS. Not for showing up, not for hours, not for good intentions.
steps.trusted: Building more, and helping the next person get their first contribution in.

steps.line: You've built it, so you can check it.
steps.how: You've had work merged and you want the responsibility, so you ask. The Lab's stewards decide based on the quality of what you've built.
steps.trusted: Reviewing changes in the areas you've built in, and helping people get their work ready.

steps.how: Your reviews and your own work have held up. You ask, and the Lab's stewards decide.
steps.trusted: Merging reviewed changes into the Lab's OLOS, and mentoring Reviewers.

steps.line: You look after the whole of it.
steps.how: You've helped shape the Lab's OLOS across the board. You ask, and the other Maintainers decide.
steps.trusted: Deciding where the Lab's OLOS goes next, and looking after the people who look after it.

rings.names: If the answer is "not yet", the stewards tell you specifically what would change it. Stewards shape the system through review; the boards still look after money, people and the brand.

picker.stageLabel: The {rank} pin. Drag, or use the arrow keys, to turn it.
alts: The gold pin with one ring, for a Reviewer
The gold pin with two rings, for a Committer
The gold pin with three rings, for a Maintainer

given.kicker: How the gold pin is given
given.title: Our version of graduation.

steps.title: Learn to build.
steps.body: In a Build Cycle, in your role, with someone pairing with you.

steps.title: Get something in.
steps.body: Reviewed and merged into the Lab's OLOS, and the Lab runs on it.

steps.title: It goes on the record.
steps.body: One line about what you built, next to your name, in the Lab's OLOS.

steps.title: Pinned.
steps.body: At the next big get-together in your region, in front of everyone, by the people who reviewed your work.

given.note: There's no clock on any of this. Some people get there in their first cycle, some take longer. Every role is on the path.

status.title: Once it's yours, it stays yours.
status.lede: Your pin and your rings don't go away. The only question is whether you're doing the work right now.

items.label: Active
items.title: In the thick of it.
items.body: You're reviewing, merging or maintaining, and you have the say that comes with it.

items.label: Emeritus
items.title: Taking a step back.
items.body: You keep your pin, your rings and your voice. When you're ready, come on back.

core.kicker: From one Lab to every Lab
core.title: The best of it ends up in every Lab.
core.lede: HQ maintains the core: the shared OLOS every Lab starts from. It drives the major updates, rebuilds and new features. And it grows from what each Lab has proven.

steps.title: It works in the Lab.
steps.body: It's merged, the Lab runs on it, and you've seen what it changed.

steps.title: It's proposed to the core.
steps.body: The Lab's stewards put it forward. They know your work and they've seen it run.

steps.title: It's reviewed for every Lab.
steps.body: National stewards check that it works beyond the place it was built, and work with you on what needs to change.

steps.title: Every Lab gets it.
steps.body: Merged into the core, with your name and the Lab's on it. That's the nickel pin.

core.note: It's the same system, one level up. Nickel pins, and national Reviewers, Committers and Maintainers, work just like they do in a Lab.

decides.title: A few things that won't change.
rules: The people who build and look after OLOS shape it, through review. Nothing goes in unreviewed, and no one acts alone.
The boards look after the organization: money, people, legal and the brand.
No one can buy a pin, a ring, or a vote. Only the work counts.
The only way to lose a pin or a ring is to seriously break the Code of Conduct.

join.title: Every pin starts with your first contribution.
join.lede: The simplest way to start is the ambassador program. Share your story, bring someone to their first workshop, and see what you end up building.

footer.renders: Images of the pin are 3D renders, not photos. The real pins are still being made.
